source.title: Optic nerve aplasia: A case series
source.design: three pediatric optic nerve aplasia case reports without comparator or analytic cohort

extraction_metadata.scope_note: The three primary cases, clinically important observations, author conclusions, consent, funding, and conflict disclosures were atomized. Background claims from cited literature were generally excluded. One historical literature-count statement was retained as secondary synthesis and tagged accordingly. Bibliographic entries were not atomized.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report three cases of optic nerve aplasia with different clinical presentations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report three cases of ONA with varied clinical presentations.

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 was a 6-year-old girl with apparent small size and intermittent deviation of the right eye since birth.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 6-year-old girl, born to a nonconsanguineous marriage, was brought in with the complaints of apparent small size with occasional deviation of the right eye since birth.

population.label: Case 1: 6-year-old girl with unilateral right optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: In Case 1, the right eye had no perception of light, pseudoptosis, and a total afferent pupillary defect, while the left eye had 20/20 vision and normal clinical findings.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Examination revealed absent perception of light, pseudoptosis, and total afferent pupillary defect (TAPD) in the right eye. The left eye had vision 20/20 with normal clinical findings.

population.label: Case 1: 6-year-old girl with unilateral right optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 1 had 50 prism diopters of right exotropia and relative right enophthalmos, with Leudde exophthalmometry measuring 8 mm in the right eye and 10 mm in the left eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The right eye had 50 prism diopters exotropia with modified Krimsky. Exophthalmometry by Leudde’s measured 8 mm (right eye), 10 mm (left eye) suggestive of enophthalmos of the right eye.

population.label: Case 1: 6-year-old girl with unilateral right optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Fundus examination in Case 1 showed complete absence of the right optic nerve and retinal vessels, chorioretinal atrophic patches, and a highly tessellated background retina; the left fundus was normal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fundus examination of the right eye showed a complete absence of the optic nerve and retinal blood vessels with chorioretinal atrophic patches and a highly tessellated background retina. The left eye fundus was within normal limits.

population.label: Case 1: 6-year-old girl with unilateral right optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Imaging in Case 1 supported absence of the orbital right optic nerve, while no significant brain anomaly was identified.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No significant anomaly of the brain was noted. T1 weighted, coronal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed complete absence of the optic nerve in the right eye in the expected location in the intraconal fat, thus confirming the absence of the orbital part of the optic nerve.

population.label: Case 1: 6-year-old girl with unilateral right optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 was a 5-year-old child with no vision in a small-appearing left eye since birth and a history of trauma and surgery to the right eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 5-year-old child with unremarkable birth history was brought in with the complaints of having no vision in the left eye which appeared small in size since birth. There was a past history of trauma with stone and ocular surgery in the right eye.

population.label: Case 2: 5-year-old child with unilateral left optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: In Case 2, the left eye had no perception of light, a vertically 12 mm by horizontally 9 mm cornea, and partial aniridia from 7 to 2 o’clock.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On examination, best-corrected visual acuity in the right eye was 20/40 with Cardiff cards and no perception of light in the left eye. Left eye corneal diameter was 12 mm vertically and 9 mm horizontally. There was partial aniridia from 7 to 2 o’ clock hours.

population.label: Case 2: 5-year-old child with unilateral left optic nerve aplasia

concept.text: Left-eye visual and anterior segment findings

atoms.canonical_statement: Fundus examination in Case 2 showed complete absence of the left optic nerve and retinal vessels with chorioretinal atrophy in the macula and mid-peripheral retina.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fundus examination revealed the complete absence of the optic nerve and retinal vessels and areas of chorioretinal atrophy in the macula and mid-peripheral retina.

population.label: Case 2: 5-year-old child with unilateral left optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 2 had intraocular pressure of 50 mmHg in the left eye and 12 mmHg in the right eye by applanation tonometry.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Intraocular pressure was 12 mmHg in the right eye and 50 mmHg in the left eye by applanation tonometry.

population.label: Case 2: 5-year-old child with unilateral left optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 was a 5-month-old girl who had not developed a social smile; she was born at term after an uneventful perinatal period and had normal general and systemic examinations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 5-month-old girl child was brought with a complaint of not having developed social smile. This child was born to a nonconsanguineous marriage by normal term delivery with an uneventful perinatal period. General and systemic examinations were within normal limits.

population.label: Case 3: 5-month-old girl with bilateral optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: Case 3 did not fix or follow light and had bilateral microcornea, a persistent pupillary membrane in the right eye, and typical iris and lens coloboma in the left eye.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: On ocular examination, the child was not fixing or following the light. There was microcornea in both the eyes with the persistent pupillary membrane in the right eye and typical iris coloboma with lens coloboma in the left eye.

population.label: Case 3: 5-month-old girl with bilateral optic nerve aplasia

concept.text: Visual behavior and anterior segment morphology

atoms.canonical_statement: Fundus examination in Case 3 showed absent optic nerve heads and retinal blood vessels in both eyes with tessellated background retina.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Fundus examination revealed clear media with absent optic nerve head and retinal blood vessels and tessellated background retina in both the eyes.

population.label: Case 3: 5-month-old girl with bilateral optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: MRI in Case 3 showed bilateral absence of the optic nerves and chiasm without a brain abnormality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: MRI revealed the bilateral absence of optic nerves and chiasma and no abnormality of the brain.

population.label: Case 3: 5-month-old girl with bilateral optic nerve aplasia

concept.text: Optic nerves, chiasm, and brain imaging

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that their literature review identified 38 reported cases of optic nerve aplasia at the time of publication.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Literature review has revealed 38 cases of ONA being reported till date.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors characterize the third case as unusual because brain imaging was normal despite bilateral optic nerve aplasia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The third was unique in that, CNS was within normal limits in spite of bilaterality.

population.label: Case 3: 5-month-old girl with bilateral optic nerve aplasia

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors state that optic nerve aplasia has poor visual prognosis and direct management toward identifying associated systemic abnormalities.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The prognosis of ONA is poor and management is directed towards identifying any associated systemic abnormality.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend thorough systemic evaluation and neuroimaging in children with optic nerve aplasia to assess for central nervous system malformations and endocrinological abnormalities.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A thorough systemic evaluation along with neuroimaging is recommended in children with ONA to rule out CNS malformations and endocrinological abnormalities.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend ocular prosthesis for esthesis, shatterproof glasses, mobility training, and vocational rehabilitation to support social development.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Ocular prosthesis for esthesis and shatterproof glasses along with mobility training and vocational rehabilitation are recommended for optimized social development.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report obtaining appropriate patient consent for publication of images and clinical information.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The authors certify that they have obtained all appropriate patient consent forms.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report no financial support or sponsorship.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Financial support and sponsorship Nil.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report no conflicts of interest.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: There are no conflicts of interest.
